extracted.intended_audience: postdoctoral researchers applying for Marie Skłodowska-Curie Actions Postdoctoral Fellowships (MSCA-PF)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for preparing Parts A, B1 and B2 of an MSCA Postdoctoral Fellowship (MSCA-PF) application, with emphasis on the evaluated B1 section (Excellence, Impact, Implementation) and the supporting B2 documentation. Focused on maximizing evaluation scores and feasibility within the fellowship timeframe.

rubrics_metrics.name: Part A — Administrative documentation
rubrics_metrics.description: This part is mainly administrative. It includes documentation that has to be filled online.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure all required administrative fields and uploads are complete and correct in the online form; missing or incorrect administrative information can invalidate or delay evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Excellence — ambitious, feasible, measurable research objectives
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe ambitious research objectives that go beyond the state-of-the-art of your research area but are also feasible and measurable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not be overambitious; propose research that can be realistically completed within the fellowship timeframe. Be explicit about what 'beyond state-of-the-art' means in measurable terms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Excellence — appropriate methodology
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe an appropriate methodology to deliver the proposed objectives in the timeframe of the proposal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Show methodological rigor and feasibility; an interdisciplinary approach is a plus. Explain methods, why they are suitable, timeline alignment, and any pilot data or preliminary work that supports feasibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Excellence — gender dimension (if applicable)
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe the gender dimension aspects, if applicable to your research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If relevant, explain how sex/gender analysis or gender-aware design is integrated into research questions, methods, and dissemination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Excellence — open science practices
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe how you plan to ensure open science practices throughout the fellowship.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detail plans for data management, sharing protocols, preprints, open access publishing, code and materials sharing, and compliance with funder/institutional open science policies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Excellence — supervisor qualifications and experience
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe how the qualifications and experience of the supervisor(s) ensure an adequate supervision of the project (i.e., experience on the proposed research topic, track record, main collaborations, and experience training researchers at an advanced level).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide concrete evidence of supervisor expertise, relevant collaborations, previous successful supervision of postdocs, and how supervisory input will support project milestones and training.

rubrics_metrics.name: Excellence — applicant's research experience relevance
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe how the applicant’s research experience will help develop the proposed research objectives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain how the applicant's prior work, skills, and achievements position them to deliver the proposed research and how gaps will be addressed through training and supervision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Excellence — specific training activities
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe specific training activities for the researcher in both scientific and technical competences, as well as in transferrable and management skills.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List concrete training events, secondments, courses, supervision plans, and timelines showing how the fellowship will develop the researcher’s capabilities and career prospects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Excellence — knowledge transfer actions
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe how the transfer of knowledge between the researcher and the host(s) organisations will be ensured with specific actions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detail mechanisms for mutual knowledge exchange (e.g., joint seminars, secondments, co-supervision, collaborative experiments) and expected outcomes for both researcher and host.

rubrics_metrics.name: Impact — development of new competences and career impact
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe the expected development of new competences of the applicant and the expected fellowship’s impact on the applicant’s career perspective inside and/or outside academia.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be explicit about skill gains, career pathways enabled by the fellowship, and how these are realistic and matched to the applicant’s profile and market/academic needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Impact — communication and dissemination strategy
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe specific actions to communicate and disseminate your project’s results, maximising their impact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design a strategy for dissemination to the scientific community (publications, conferences, networks) and for public engagement activities to reach broader society. These activities may include outreach on topics beyond project-specific results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Impact — intellectual property management plan (if applicable)
rubrics_metrics.description: Design and describe a plan for the management and protection of intellectual property (if this is applicable to the proposed project).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include IP ownership, filing strategy, exploitation routes, and partner/host support for IP protection where relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Impact — realistic description of expected broader impacts
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe the expected scientific, technological, economic, and societal impact of the project beyond the immediate scope of the project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be realistic — evaluators do not expect transformative global claims in two years. Provide plausible, evidence-based pathways to impact and indicators to judge progress.

rubrics_metrics.name: Implementation — work plan, deliverables and milestones
rubrics_metrics.description: Briefly describe an organisational structure of the work plan and define deliverables and milestones.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Structure the work packages, tasks, responsibilities, and outputs clearly. Deliverables and milestones should be specific, measurable, and linked to the methodology and timeline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Implementation — Gantt chart and timeline feasibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Present the timeline of the work plan in a Gantt chart that is feasible, realistic, and logical.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a clear schedule that aligns tasks, training, dissemination and any secondments; avoid unrealistic concurrency and overambitious sequencing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Implementation — risk assessment, contingency and monitoring
rubrics_metrics.description: Include the assessment of risks of the project, the corresponding contingency plans to mitigate these risks, and the monitoring mechanisms to ensure the correct development of the project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify key risks, mitigation strategies, and monitoring processes (e.g., periodic meetings with supervisor(s), performance indicators) to demonstrate adaptive management.

rubrics_metrics.name: Implementation — hosting arrangements and integration
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe the hosting arrangements, the integration in the team/institution and support services, and the capacity of the participating organisations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain how the host will integrate the researcher (office/lab space, induction, mentoring), what support services are available, and how the host environment contributes to project success.

rubrics_metrics.name: Part B2 — applicant CV content
rubrics_metrics.description: The applicant’s CV (≈5 pages) including publications, conferences, research expeditions, patents, prizes, funding, supervising activities, and others.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a concise, relevant CV highlighting achievements and experience directly supporting the proposed project and training objectives; keep length guidance in mind (~5 pages).

rubrics_metrics.name: Part B2 — capacity of participating organisations
rubrics_metrics.description: Profile of the supervisor, infrastructure, facilities and equipment, and involvement in EU-funded research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document institutional capabilities, relevant facilities, past participation in EU projects, and how these resources will support the fellowship activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Part B2 — commitment of associated partners (if applicable)
rubrics_metrics.description: Commitment of the associated partner(s), if applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include letters or statements of commitment detailing the partner’s role, resources, and contributions to training, secondments or project tasks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balanced proposal — address all B1 points with concrete actions
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not only prioritise writing an attractive and ambitious research project disregarding the other sections; build a well-rounded proposal for the B1 section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cover and answer all points in Part B1 with concrete actions that give credibility and feasibility to the proposal (Excellence, Impact, Implementation). Evaluators assess both scientific quality and long-term impact on host, group, applicant and society.

rubrics_metrics.name: Feasibility indicators — demonstrate realistic implementation within timeframe
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluators will look for indicators of the feasibility of the proposed implementation of the project within the timeframe of the fellowship.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide realistic schedules, prior evidence, resource availability, supervisory support, and risk/contingency plans to demonstrate you can achieve objectives in the fellowship period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Misconception to avoid — publication record is not the sole determinant
rubrics_metrics.description: You do not necessarily need an outstanding publication record to be awarded a MSCA-PF (the evaluators consider the applicant’s career stage).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus on fit between proposal and your research profile, supervisor suitability, and how the fellowship will develop key skills and expertise rather than only on publication counts.
